name: VictoriaMetrics
model: Prometheus-compatible metric time series; accepts Prometheus remote write, Influx line protocol and more; MetricsQL (a PromQL superset)
engine_note: Custom LSM-like, MergeTree-inspired store: in-memory parts flushed to immutable on-disk parts, merged in background per monthly partition; no WAL
consistency: No transactions. No write-ahead log: the last few seconds of inserted data (in-memory parts, flushed every few seconds) can be lost on a hard crash; new samples become queryable after up to a few seconds.
scaling: Single binary scales up well; the cluster version is shared-nothing: vminsert, vmstorage and vmselect scale separately, data sharded across vmstorage nodes, optional replication.
licence: Apache License 2.0 (open-source single-node and cluster); Enterprise edition under a commercial licence
reach: Reach for it as long-term, cheaper-to-run storage for Prometheus metrics, or when one Prometheus runs out of memory on high-cardinality series.
avoid: Avoid when losing a few seconds of samples on a crash is unacceptable, or you want storage on object storage rather than local disks.
escape: Metrics outgrow one Prometheus; it stores them compactly on local disks with PromQL-compatible queries.
chat: Long-term store for all service metrics, fed by Prometheus remote write, kept for a year.
notes: Quotes: 'The last few seconds of inserted data may be lost on unclean shutdown (i.e. OOM, kill -9 or hardware reset). The -inmemoryDataFlushInterval command-line flag allows controlling the frequency of in-memory data flush to persistent storage.'; 'VictoriaMetrics puts the recently ingested samples into in-memory buffers, which aren't available for querying for up to a few seconds.'; 'These compactions (merges) are performed independently on per-month partitions.' MergeTree/ClickHouse inspiration is from the VictoriaMetrics author's articles (not quoted this session). Enterprise commercial licence and VictoriaMetrics Cloud named from vendor site, not re-fetched. No Jepsen analysis.
